DIAGNOSIS READY: Frontotemporal Dementia with possible associated neurological decline.

The patient presents with a 6-month history of cognitive decline (forgetfulness, getting lost) and behavioral changes (paranoia, agitation), followed by a more acute 1-week onset of right leg weakness and falls. This rapid neurological deterioration suggests a superimposed condition such as a stroke or tumor affecting the frontal/temporal lobes or motor pathways, potentially complicating an underlying neurodegenerative process.
